validated_work_order.confidence_rationale: Every surviving finding was reproduced on the current head by a full-suite mutation sweep, and the single new test was written and executed against five separate mutations before this order was written — it fails under all five and passes clean. The two dropped findings were dropped on executed evidence (the code already does what the finding asked for), not on a reading of the diff. The only judgement call left is prose in a doc comment, and the fallback behaviour it documents is already pinned by a test.
validated_work_order.understanding: Issue #44 carries eight non-blocking findings from the review of #43 and asks that each be re-checked against the merged file before it is planned. Re-checking the current head (271 tests, all green) gives two different answers. Two of the eight no longer reproduce: the eight-key wire contract (finding at src/data/repositories.js:595) and the two-of-eight seed predicate (scripts/seed.js:319) were both fixed after the review was written. src/data/repositories.js:596 now calls the domain's readableComponents(), which derives the projection from COMPONENTS and therefore always emits all eight keys, and scripts/seed.js:332 gates on isReadableOpportunityRecord(), which is now unreadableComponents(record).length === 0 — every key, not two. Both are pinned by test/domain/opportunity-readability.test.js and test/ops/seed.test.js, including the half-migrated row the reviewer planted by hand. Implementing either would be a no-op dressed as a fix. The other six reproduce, and five of them are the same defect seen from six angles: the tenant currency is threaded at fourteen render sites in src/web/pages.js and only three of them can be caught by a test. I mutated each site in isolation against the whole suite; these five are mutation-invisible — experimentCard's two money() calls (pages.js:772), both cards.map(experimentCard) call sites in experiments() (pages.js:827 and :843), the partial branch of opportunities() (pages.js:738), the partial branch of dashboard() (pages.js:320) and the Qualified CPL tile in kpiStrip (pages.js:384). Every one of them renders a rupee for a USD tenant the moment its `tenant?.currency ?? 'INR'` is dropped, and no test fails. The cause is one shape, not six: the only non-INR tenant fixture in the suite renders /opportunities and / with no state override, so it lands on the ideal branch and the INR branch of experimentCard's caps and never on the partial branches, and no non-INR tenant has any events at all, so the CPL tile is always the em-dash. The sixth is documentation: a comment at test/web/pages.test.js:951 claims the two cards.map sites and both caps are guarded, which is exactly the coverage that does not exist; a comment at test/api/opportunities.test.js:41-43 gives 2026-09-25 for a constant that is 2026-09-10; and the doc comment above money() at src/web/pages.js:197-211 justifies its unknown-currency fallback only as a 500-avoidance, without saying the amount on screen is relabelled as rupees. So the whole change is one test file plus two comment corrections: no production behaviour moves.
validated_work_order.root_cause: Currency coverage is sampled from one tenant and one state, so it can only ever exercise the ideal branch of the pages that have one. Six of the fourteen currency-threading sites in src/web/pages.js are reachable only under `override: 'partial'` or from a tenant with a non-zero qualified volume, and the suite had no fixture meeting either condition, so the coverage claim in the work order and in the test's own comment was never checked by anything.
validated_work_order.approach: Add one test to test/web/pages.test.js that closes all five invisible sites with a single USD-tenant fixture, and correct three comments. The new test is named for what it pins rather than for the page it renders. Fixture: a fresh database, a `tenant_usd` tenant with currency 'USD', one opportunity (value_micros 6_000_000_000, cost_micros 1_900_000_000, and the other six components in range), one experiment with caps {max_spend_micros: 500_000_000, max_downside_micros: 200_000_000}, and — the part the existing USD fixture lacks — one `spend.observed` of 3_000_000_000 USD plus one `lead_qualified`, appended through `repositories.rawEvents.append` after `validateEvent` so qualified CPL resolves to $3,000.00 and the CPL tile renders a number instead of the em-dash. Assertions, each scoped so it can only be satisfied by the site it guards: (a) `/opportunities` with `override: 'partial'` — the opportunity row carries `value $6,000.00` and `cost $1,900.00` and no `₹`; (b) `/experiments` with no override and again with `override: 'partial'` — the card's `data-testid="caps"` element reads `Max spend $500.00 · max downside $200.00` exactly and the card holds no `₹`; (c) `/` with no override and again with `override: 'partial'`, passing a `FakeMetaAdsProvider` — the CPL tile's `kpi-value` is exactly `$3,000.00`, and the `data-testid="meta-adSets"` and `data-testid="meta-insights"` sections carry `$500.00` and `$4,000.00` and no `₹`. Every render is the ideal-plus-partial pair, because a mutation at either branch of the same call site has to be caught and only the pair catches both. The Meta assertions are scoped to their own `[data-testid]` sections rather than to the whole document, because the CPL value and the insight spend would otherwise let each other's regression pass; this follows .sdlc/memory/qa/selectors.md, which is why those testids are asserted rather than class names. No new fixture file, no new helper, no production change: the five sites are already correct, and the whole point of the finding is that nothing was checking them. The test's leading comment names the five guarded sites by function and branch — experimentCard, both cards.map sites in experiments(), the partial branch of opportunities(), the partial branch of dashboard(), the Qualified CPL tile — and deliberately carries no line numbers, since the #43 work order's line numbers were already stale by ~18 when this issue was filed and a comment that names lines goes stale the same way. The comment says what the test proves and nothing more, which is the defect finding 4 of the six was about. Separately: the comment at test/web/pages.test.js:951 loses its coverage claim only if the new test does not make it true, so after this change it is accurate and stays as it is; the FROZEN_INSTANT_MS comment at test/api/opportunities.test.js:41-43 is corrected from 2026-09-25T12:00:00Z to 2026-09-10T12:00:00Z, and a small test reads that file's own source and asserts the date in the comment equals `new Date(FROZEN_INSTANT_MS).toISOString().slice(0, 10)`, so the comment cannot drift from the constant again — the same source-reading pattern the h1 tests at the end of pages.test.js already use. The doc comment above money() at src/web/pages.js:197-211 keeps the fallback exactly as it is and adds the sentence it was missing: a currency outside ISO_CURRENCIES renders as INR, so a tenant whose stored currency is bad data reads its amounts in rupees rather than in its own code, and that is a deliberate choice rather than an oversight. The behaviour is unchanged and stays pinned by the existing test 'an unrecognised tenant currency renders as INR instead of throwing'.

Leading comment on the new test: name the five sites it guards by function and branch (experimentCard's two money() calls, both cards.map(experimentCard) sites in experiments(), the partial branch of opportunities(), the partial branch of dashboard(), the Qualified CPL tile in kpiStrip), state that each is dropped individually by its own assertion, and state explicitly that the comment carries no line numbers because a line-numbered coverage claim is what went stale in the #43 work order. Leave the existing comment at the top of 'the experiment caps render through the same helper on both the ideal and the partial branch' as it is — this change is what makes it true.

risks: The new test hardcodes a rendered CPL string ('$3,000.00') and a pair of Meta figures ('$500.00', '$4,000.00'). Those come from FakeMetaAdsProvider and from the fixture, both of which are stable today, but a change to the fake provider's row counts or amounts would break the test for a reason that has nothing to do with currency. The failure message should therefore name the site, not just the string.

The CPL assertion depends on the two appended events. If a future change makes lead_qualified rows require a matching spend.observed campaign or a journey link, the fixture stops producing a qualified volume and the CPL tile silently returns the em-dash — and the assertion fails with '$3,000.00' versus '—', which reads as a currency bug when it is a fixture bug. The qualified-volume assertion placed early in the test is what distinguishes the two.

src/web/pages.js is touched for a comment only. The risk is a well-meaning implementer 'tidying' the money() ternary into a pass-through while the comment is being written, which would be a behaviour change to every amount on every screen and would silently break the existing ZZZ fallback test's intent. The existing test would catch it, but the review should check the diff hunk count rather than trust the PR title.

out_of_scope: The eight-key wire contract at src/data/repositories.js:595 — already fixed on this head. shape() now calls the domain's readableComponents(), which derives the projection from COMPONENTS and always emits all eight keys; a record with only name, value_micros and cost_micros serialises as eight keys with six nulls, verified by execution on this head and pinned by test/domain/opportunity-readability.test.js. The finding's own proposed fix (extend the projection to all eight) is what the code already does, and its second option (narrow the wording) is unnecessary because the wording now matches the code.

approved_work_order.understanding: Issue #44 carries eight non-blocking findings from the review of #43 and asks that each be re-checked against the merged file before it is planned. Re-checking the current head (271 tests, all green) gives two different answers. Two of the eight no longer reproduce: the eight-key wire contract (finding at src/data/repositories.js:595) and the two-of-eight seed predicate (scripts/seed.js:319) were both fixed after the review was written. src/data/repositories.js:596 now calls the domain's readableComponents(), which derives the projection from COMPONENTS and therefore always emits all eight keys, and scripts/seed.js:332 gates on isReadableOpportunityRecord(), which is now unreadableComponents(record).length === 0 — every key, not two. Both are pinned by test/domain/opportunity-readability.test.js and test/ops/seed.test.js, including the half-migrated row the reviewer planted by hand. Implementing either would be a no-op dressed as a fix. The other six reproduce, and five of them are the same defect seen from six angles: the tenant currency is threaded at fourteen render sites in src/web/pages.js and only three of them can be caught by a test. I mutated each site in isolation against the whole suite; these five are mutation-invisible — experimentCard's two money() calls (pages.js:772), both cards.map(experimentCard) call sites in experiments() (pages.js:827 and :843), the partial branch of opportunities() (pages.js:738), the partial branch of dashboard() (pages.js:320) and the Qualified CPL tile in kpiStrip (pages.js:384). Every one of them renders a rupee for a USD tenant the moment its `tenant?.currency ?? 'INR'` is dropped, and no test fails. The cause is one shape, not six: the only non-INR tenant fixture in the suite renders /opportunities and / with no state override, so it lands on the ideal branch and the INR branch of experimentCard's caps and never on the partial branches, and no non-INR tenant has any events at all, so the CPL tile is always the em-dash. The sixth is documentation: a comment at test/web/pages.test.js:951 claims the two cards.map sites and both caps are guarded, which is exactly the coverage that does not exist; a comment at test/api/opportunities.test.js:41-43 gives 2026-09-25 for a constant that is 2026-09-10; and the doc comment above money() at src/web/pages.js:197-211 justifies its unknown-currency fallback only as a 500-avoidance, without saying the amount on screen is relabelled as rupees. So the whole change is one test file plus two comment corrections: no production behaviour moves.
approved_work_order.root_cause: Currency coverage is sampled from one tenant and one state, so it can only ever exercise the ideal branch of the pages that have one. Six of the fourteen currency-threading sites in src/web/pages.js are reachable only under `override: 'partial'` or from a tenant with a non-zero qualified volume, and the suite had no fixture meeting either condition, so the coverage claim in the work order and in the test's own comment was never checked by anything.
approved_work_order.approach: Add one test to test/web/pages.test.js that closes all five invisible sites with a single USD-tenant fixture, and correct three comments. The new test is named for what it pins rather than for the page it renders. Fixture: a fresh database, a `tenant_usd` tenant with currency 'USD', one opportunity (value_micros 6_000_000_000, cost_micros 1_900_000_000, and the other six components in range), one experiment with caps {max_spend_micros: 500_000_000, max_downside_micros: 200_000_000}, and — the part the existing USD fixture lacks — one `spend.observed` of 3_000_000_000 USD plus one `lead_qualified`, appended through `repositories.rawEvents.append` after `validateEvent` so qualified CPL resolves to $3,000.00 and the CPL tile renders a number instead of the em-dash. Assertions, each scoped so it can only be satisfied by the site it guards: (a) `/opportunities` with `override: 'partial'` — the opportunity row carries `value $6,000.00` and `cost $1,900.00` and no `₹`; (b) `/experiments` with no override and again with `override: 'partial'` — the card's `data-testid="caps"` element reads `Max spend $500.00 · max downside $200.00` exactly and the card holds no `₹`; (c) `/` with no override and again with `override: 'partial'`, passing a `FakeMetaAdsProvider` — the CPL tile's `kpi-value` is exactly `$3,000.00`, and the `data-testid="meta-adSets"` and `data-testid="meta-insights"` sections carry `$500.00` and `$4,000.00` and no `₹`. Every render is the ideal-plus-partial pair, because a mutation at either branch of the same call site has to be caught and only the pair catches both. The Meta assertions are scoped to their own `[data-testid]` sections rather than to the whole document, because the CPL value and the insight spend would otherwise let each other's regression pass; this follows .sdlc/memory/qa/selectors.md, which is why those testids are asserted rather than class names. The comment says what the test proves and nothing more, which is the defect finding 4 of the six was about. Separately: the comment at test/web/pages.test.js:951 loses its coverage claim only if the new test does not make it true, so after this change it is accurate and stays as it is; the FROZEN_INSTANT_MS comment at test/api/opportunities.test.js:41-43 is corrected from 2026-09-25T12:00:00Z to 2026-09-10T12:00:00Z, and a small test reads that file's own source and asserts the date in the comment equals `new Date(FROZEN_INSTANT_MS).toISOString().slice(0, 10)`, so the comment cannot drift from the constant again — the same source-reading pattern the h1 tests at the end of pages.test.js already use.
